_about: Field terms for F14, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

newtons-rings.definition: the bright and dark circles seen where a curved lens rests on flat glass, made by light reflected from the two faces of the thin air gap between them, whose thickness grows with distance from the point of contact
newtons-rings.excludes: rings made by diffraction at an edge or an aperture

obliquity.definition: the angle between the light's path and the perpendicular to the glass; Newton's table gives it twice, once inside the glass and once in the air gap
obliquity.excludes: the tilt of the glass itself, which stays fixed

secant-law.definition: the statement that the air thickness at which a given ring appears grows as one over the cosine of the light's angle in the air gap, scaled here so that perpendicular light gives 10
secant-law.excludes: any rule built from the angle in the glass

means-rule.field: history of optics; Newton's own rule in Opticks, Book II
means-rule.definition: Newton's statement that the thickness goes as the secant of an angle whose sine is the first of 106 arithmetical means between the sines of incidence and refraction, counted from the bigger sine
means-rule.excludes: the secant law, which uses the air angle alone

airy-reflectance.definition: the share of light power a thin layer reflects when every reflected and re-reflected beam inside it is summed, rather than only the first two
airy-reflectance.excludes: the two-beam approximation, and absorption in the glass

polarisation.definition: the two directions of the light's electric field relative to the plane that holds the ray and the perpendicular to the surface: s across that plane and p within it; unpolarised light is their average
polarisation.excludes: circular polarisation, which this study does not model

half-wave-flip.definition: the change of sign of the reflected wave at one face of the air gap and not the other, which makes the centre of the rings dark in reflected light
half-wave-flip.excludes: the phase delay from the path across the gap

d65.definition: a standard table of the power in average midday daylight at each wavelength, used as the white light in this study
d65.excludes: the measured spectrum of any one day's sunlight, and Newton's own light

luminance-y.definition: the brightness of light as the standard eye weighs it, computed by weighting power at each wavelength with the CIE 1931 2 degree observer's brightness curve
luminance-y.excludes: hue and saturation, which the study does not score
